title: Series: observations over slot history
preamble:
# Series: observations over slot history

Series declarations name the
**observations** an author wants on a slot's history —
aggregations, time models, accuracy bounds — and the compiler
picks the backing structures.

Paired with:
- [LGRA] — the series declaration grammar.
- [LEXP] — aggregation calls are
  atoms in expression grammar; compose freely with
  arithmetic.
- [LFAC] — the no-op reassertion
  discipline that meaningful-change series updates depend on.

## What this is not

- Not the series declaration grammar — see
  [LGRA].
- Not a dwell spec — `t.dwell` is a compile-time alias for
  the time since the fact entered working memory on `logical`-schema bindings, unrelated to
  series maintenance. See [LFAC].
- Not a runtime-implementation guide. Welford running stats,
  ring-buffer and deque sizing, trailing-tail buffer sizes,
  memory accounting — those are the runtime's
  ([ISBK]).
- Not a backing implementation guide. Which backing serves
  each observation triple is catalogued in [LSER.18.1]; how
  each one is built (running-stats, monotonic deque, ring
  buffer, reservoir) is the runtime's business.
